x: Nirguna is the Bhakti idea of the formless one God (Kabir, Nanak), and Tawhid is the Sufi doctrine of God's oneness, so 'Bhakti — Nirguna; Sufism — Tawhid' is right. Option A reverses the pair, Wahdat-ul-Wujud in B is a Sufi (not Bhakti) doctrine, and the maqamat in D are Sufi stations while Padavali kirtans are Bengali Bhakti songs.

The order is Nanak, Angad, Amar Das, Ram Das, Arjan Dev, Hargobind, Har Rai, Har Krishan, Tegh Bahadur, Gobind Singh. The other options swap pairs such as Angad/Amar Das, Ram Das/Amar Das, Hargobind/Har Rai or Har Krishan/Har Rai, or put Tegh Bahadur after Gobind Singh.

The order of arrival is Portuguese (1498), Dutch (first factory Masulipatnam 1605), English (Surat farman 1613), Danes (Tranquebar 1620) and French (Surat 1668). The trap is option B, which follows company formation (English 1600 before Dutch 1602) rather than arrival.
Tobacco is one of the New World crops the Portuguese brought to India, along with potato, chilli, maize, pineapple, papaya, cashew and groundnut. Rubber, tea and coffee are not in that list.
Tobacco, chilli and tomato (to Telugu soil) are Portuguese introductions. Wheat is the wrong pair: it is not a New World crop and is not among the crops the Portuguese introduced.

Draksharama was one of the subordinate Dutch factories in the Krishna–Godavari weaving belt. Colachel was the 1741 battle where Travancore defeated the Dutch, Batavia was the VOC's Asian headquarters, and Bantam was where de Houtman reached in 1596.

The Portuguese lost Cochin to the Dutch in 1663. Their other losses to the Dutch were Pulicat (1610) and Nagapattinam (1658); Daman, Diu and Hugli were not lost to the Dutch (Hugli fell to Shah Jahan in 1632).
